briefing.headline: OpenAI and xAI accelerate multi-agent systems as compute race intensifies

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs continue rapid iteration on reasoning models amid surging investment and regulatory scrutiny. Multi-agent coordination and safety tooling are emerging as decisive competitive edges. DialectForge's protocol-level innovations are gaining attention in enterprise deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with advanced tool-use chains while Anthropic's Claude 4.1 shows gains in long-context reasoning. xAI's Grok-3 and DeepSeek-V3 push open-weight performance boundaries. Meta open-sourced new Llama variant for research.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize runtime monitoring for agentic systems.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA ships Blackwell clusters to Microsoft and Google while TSMC ramps 2nm production for custom ASICs. Hyperscalers announce $45B in new data center builds focused on AI training.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will protocol-level security like dynamic dialects become mandatory for all frontier model deployments by 2027?
